extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level, multi-discipline tasks that require expert-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It contains 11.5K questions across six disciplines, 30 subjects, and many heterogeneous image types with interleaved text and images.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection took three stages: first, the authors selected 30 subjects from six disciplines based on common university majors and the presence of visual inputs; second, they recruited over 50 university students (including co-authors) as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources and to create new questions when necessary; third, the authors cleaned the data by removing duplicates, checking format/typos, and filtering out overly easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from major textbooks, online resources, lecture materials, and online sources; the benchmark also includes questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU has limitations despite its comprehensive nature; its focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. It also uses multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is positioned as a step toward evaluating Expert AGI and assessing capabilities across professional domains, with strong performance proposed as a necessary criterion for such systems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: A benchmark for evaluating LMMs/Expert AGI across basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities in professional domains; it combines multiple-choice and concise open-ended questions to assess diverse subjects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by author review to eliminate duplicates; format and typo checking with necessary corrections; and exclusion of about 10% of very easy problems not aligning with design criteria.
